claims.text: The starting feedstock is gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder with a particle size of 10–50 μm.
Cold spray additive manufacturing can replace laser- or electron-beam-based additive manufacturing for this feedstock.
Cold spray consolidates AlCrFeNiSi particles through high-velocity solid-state impact at temperatures below melting.
The applicable cold-spray substrate-temperature window is below 0.5 Tm of AlCrFeNiSi.
A carrier-gas temperature of 300–800°C is an applicable processing range.
The proposed process is applicable to miniature components with characteristic dimensions below 10 mm.
AlCrFeNiSi deposition requires a cold-spray system capable of particle velocities above 500 m/s.
Cold spraying will retain a nanocrystalline or as-atomized microstructure in the deposited material.
Cold spraying will avoid solidification microsegregation in AlCrFeNiSi.
Cold spraying will minimize thermal gradients and associated residual stresses.
Avoiding melting and rapid solidification eliminates the primary source of residual thermal stress and microstructural inhomogeneity.
High-velocity particle impact induces severe plastic deformation and interparticle bonding without significant heating.
Solid-state impact will prevent phase segregation and grain coarsening while preserving the feedstock microstructure.
Cold-sprayed components will have at least 50% lower residual stress than laser-powder-bed-fused counterparts.
Cold-sprayed components will have at least 20% higher ductility and lower brittleness than conventionally additively manufactured counterparts.
Cold-sprayed components will have yield strength comparable to or greater than conventionally additively manufactured counterparts.
Cold spraying will eliminate the need for preheating, post-process heat treatment, and support structures used for thermal management.
A representative LPBF baseline uses 200–400 W laser power, 500–1500 mm/s scan speed, and a 100–200°C build plate.
Conventionally LPBF-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi components exhibit residual stress and microsegregation in the as-built state.
Cold spray is not applicable to internal channels below 100 μm or to overhangs unsupported by the deposition process.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least 50% lower residual stress and 20% higher ductility, whereas the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis below 20% stress reduction or 10% ductility improvement. Results between those thresholds would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The hypothesis claims retention or preservation of the as-atomized microstructure while also claiming severe plastic deformation during impact. Severe deformation would ordinarily modify at least some feedstock microstructural features, so the meaning and extent of 'preservation' are internally unclear.
